outcomes.text: Apply foundational principles of both established and modern AI.
Build scalable algorithms and systems for practical AI applications.
Configure, train and deploy existing models for practical use.
Evaluate AI outputs and tools for reliability, efficiency, safety and goal alignment.
Use ethical and social perspectives to address AI risks and societal problems.
Communicate and collaborate across disciplines when designing AI solutions.

requirements.title: University credit and residence minimums
requirements.summary: Complete at least 120 credits, with 30 in residence, 15 at level 300+ and at least 12 in the major. Normally the final 30 are resident credits; approved study abroad/internships and at most six other credits may enter that final block with advance dean approval. Stricter major/college rules still apply.

requirements.title: Major enrollment and graduation GPA
requirements.summary: Declare a degree-granting major by 60 credits and be enrolled in the graduating major when registering for the final 15 hours. Graduation requires cumulative GPA 2.0; Fall 2012+ entrants also need 2.0 across courses satisfying each major, minor or certificate, unless the program requires more.

requirements.title: Interrupted-degree return
requirements.summary: After a registration lapse exceeding ten years, earn at least 15 new College Park credits under a department/dean-approved remaining plan, unless the authorized exception process waives that minimum.

requirements.title: Conditional second degrees and majors
requirements.summary: Only if pursuing a second degree, fulfill both programs with at least 150 credits and 18 credits unique to one degree, plus applicable residence. A second major/degree needs advance department/college approval and filed plans at least one academic year before graduation; designate the records/general-education college when two colleges are involved. A second major is not automatically a second degree.

requirements.title: General Education eligibility and overlap
requirements.summary: Use courses carrying the relevant approved General Education code for the term. Eligible courses may also meet college/major/support requirements. General Education cannot use Pass-Fail grading. These are official-designation criteria, not a fabricated fixed course pool.

requirements.title: Five Fundamental Studies areas
requirements.summary: Complete one course in each of Academic Writing, Analytic Reasoning, Mathematics, Oral Communication and Professional Writing (five courses, nominally 15 credits). Academic Writing requires C- or better. Academic Writing and Mathematics carry the source footnote requiring an attempt by 30 credits and completion by 60; do not apply that footnote to all five areas.

requirements.title: Eight Distributive Studies courses
requirements.summary: Complete two courses in each of History/Social Sciences, Humanities, Natural Sciences and Scholarship in Practice (eight courses, nominally 25 credits). One Natural Sciences course needs the designated lab experience, and one Scholarship in Practice course must be outside major requirements.

requirements.title: Big Question overlay
requirements.summary: At least two Distributive Studies courses must carry Big Question designation (formerly I-Series). This is an overlay within the eight-course distribution requirement, not two extra courses.

requirements.title: Diversity alternatives
requirements.summary: Complete either two Understanding Plural Societies courses, or one Understanding Plural Societies plus one Cultural Competence course. Approved diversity courses may also meet a Distributive Studies category.

requirements.title: Transfer acceptance versus degree applicability
requirements.summary: Transfer generally needs an equivalent college-level course and C- or better; qualifying Maryland public-institution work may transfer at D- under the stated policy. Acceptance is separate from degree applicability and its potentially higher grade minimum, which the advising college decides. Transfer grades do not enter UMD cumulative GPA.

requirements.title: Transfer-credit caps and residence
requirements.summary: For newly matriculated Fall 2022+ students, at most 70 applicable credits may come from two-year institutions. Combined four-year/prior-learning/two-year sources are capped at 90 applicable transfer credits, with at least 30 credits in UMD residence. Acceptance alone does not establish degree applicability.

requirements.title: Advance external-study permission
requirements.summary: Before external enrollment, obtain advising-college permission through PTE for U.S. study or SACA for international study after course acceptability evaluation. This applies in every term, including summer/winter. Missing advance approval can prevent acceptance or degree use; submit the official completion transcript.

requirements.title: Transfer level and conversion
requirements.summary: Transferred level follows the original course level; equivalence to a UMD upper-level code does not promote lower-level credit, and community-college work stays lower-level. The registrar converts quarter credits at .67 semester credits each without whole-number rounding. Other systems require institution-specific conversion.

requirements.title: Transfer General Education completion
requirements.summary: A documented Maryland public-community-college associate degree or completed general-education program satisfies lower General Education, subject to upper-level requirements and the 40-credit total. Documented completion at a Maryland public four-year institution satisfies General Education. A recognized completed U.S. or appropriately evaluated international bachelor degree also satisfies it. Other transfers require course-by-course application.

requirements.title: Historical transfer-writing grade exception
requirements.summary: Current Fundamental Studies Academic Writing requires C- or better. The source preserves an exception for eligible Maryland public-institution writing completed before Fall 2017 at D- or better; do not extend that historical exception to current courses.

requirements.title: Graduation application deadline
requirements.summary: File the formal graduation application at the beginning of the final semester, by its schedule-adjustment deadline; August candidates use the end of the first week of the second summer session.

requirements.title: Incomplete contract and completion
requirements.summary: An I requires satisfactory completion of most coursework and a qualifying obstacle. Submit the incomplete contract within six weeks after grade submission; complete by its deadline, normally next semester and at most one year unless the dean approves an extension. Re-registration or credit-by-exam does not remove I.

requirements.title: General Pass-Fail limits
requirements.summary: The general elective Pass-Fail option requires 30 earned college credits, including 15 at UMD, and overall/UMD GPA at least 2.0. It is limited to one course per semester and 12 career credits, cannot be chosen on repeat registration, and generally excludes college/major/GenEd requirements. ARHU separately publishes a specific language-route allowance subject to its conditions; do not apply that allowance to GenEd or a language major/minor.

requirements.title: Repeat limits and grade accounting
requirements.summary: For the stated post-Fall-1990 cohorts, a nonrepeatable course normally permits one repeat (at most two registrations after schedule adjustment) and 18 repeat credits; a dean may approve a further attempt with a success plan. Full-term withdrawal courses do not count toward the 18-credit limit. All grades normally enter GPA, with the source’s first-UMD-semester/first-24-attempted-credit higher-grade exceptions; AP credits do not enter that 24-credit count. Repeat-by-transfer follows its separate timing rule, and all attempts remain visible.

requirements.title: Gened Resources
requirements.summary: The official General Education resources page sets a minimum of 40 General Education credits even when approved requirements overlap. Nominal course-category totals are not a substitute for that minimum.

requirements.title: Cmns Advising
requirements.summary: CMNS requires membership in the graduating major before final-semester registration and addition of a double major/degree one year before graduation. This page does not name the new AI major in its program-specific declaration groups. Do not automatically assign the separate Computer Science limited-enrollment gateway to AI; AI-specific admission/transition rules remain unverified.
